new_statements.quote: В К. я. простое слово или морфема представлены главным образом сильным слогом. Возможно также сочетание сильного и слабого слогов (например, в пупео, в меньшей степени в лаха, при практическом отсутствии в гэлао). Структура сильного слога CVC или C1C2VC3. Сильный слог всегда тонирован, он ударный, занимает конечную позицию. Структура слабого слога CV, он всегда безударный и предшествует сильному; в пупео тонируется «нейтральным» ровным средним тоном, в лаха тон слабого слога повторяет этимологический тон сильного слога.
new_statements.translation: In the Kadai languages a simple word or morpheme is represented mainly by a strong syllable. A combination of a strong and a weak syllable is also possible (e.g. in Pupeo, to a lesser extent in Laha, and practically absent in Gelao). The strong syllable has the structure CVC or C1C2VC3. The strong syllable always bears tone, it is stressed, and it occupies final position. The weak syllable has the structure CV, is always unstressed and precedes the strong one; in Pupeo it carries a 'neutral' level mid tone, in Laha the tone of the weak syllable copies the etymological tone of the strong syllable.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (+.txt). With HTML tags and soft hyphens stripped, the passage beginning 'В К. я. простое слово или морфема представлены главным образом сильным слогом...' through '... в лаха тон слабого слога повторяет этимологический тон сильного слога.' is present exactly as quoted (the only rendering difference is the subscripted C1C2VC3, which extraction spaces as 'C 1 C 2 VC 3'). I also re-fetched sources the live page http://tapemark.narod.ru/les/ and it returns the same sentences, signed Н. В. Солнцева, i.e. the LES 1990 article 'Кадайские языки', p. 209. Reading: the article is a group-level typological statement for the Kadai (Kra) languages: the 'strong' syllable is always…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Tonal; the tone-bearing 'strong' syllable is the stressed one and is word-final; unstressed 'weak' CV presyllables precede it, but Gelao practically lacks such weak syllables, so a Gelao word is essentially a single stressed, tone-bearing syllable (no stress contrast inside native words; where a weak+strong disyllable occurs, stress is final).
new_statements.exceptions: Gelao is singled out as 'practically lacking' weak+strong combinations (vs. Pupeo and Laha). Note: the same article lists old prefixes lu-, qe-, qao- in Gelao, and Chinese sources (Zhang 1993, reportedly assigning prefixes a 'light tone' 轻声调) describe many prefixal syllables -- not verified here.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level typological statement for the Kadai (Kra) group with Gelao named explicitly; second-hand for Gelao (author's Gelao data from He Jiashan 1983, Wanzi/Anshun representative point, and Wang Fushi 1986); citation forms, no phrase-level discussion.
new_statements.identity_note: gela1261 is Glottolog's retired bookkeeping entry for pre-2012 'Gelao' [gio], which ISO 639-3 CR 2011-054 split into A'ou [aou] (aoua1234), Qau/Central Gelao [gqu] (qaua1234), Duoluo/White [giw] (whit1267), Red/Vandu [gir] (redg1235), Hagei/Green [giq] (gree1278), plus Mulao [giu] (gela1264); the live family node is Gelaoic gela1265. The quoted LES 1990 statement concerns 'гэлао' as described by He Jiashan 1983 (representative point Wanzi, Anshun = Central Gelao/Qau, qaua1234) and is framed at the level of the Kadai (Kra) group. Sibling audits for aoua1234, qaua1234, gela1264 and redg1235 already exist under and found no stress statement either.

sources.note: Group-level: in Kadai languages the word is mainly a single strong syllable; the strong syllable is always tone-bearing, stressed and word-final; a weak CV presyllable is always unstressed; weak+strong words occur in Pupeo, less in Laha, and are 'practically absent in Gelao'.
